business.title: Thermodynamic limit of double-junction photovoltaic cells under AM 1.5G or white LED lighting
business.description: The fundamental processes involved in charge carrier generation and recombination in ideal single- or double-junction photovoltaic cells are used to determine the thermodynamic efficiency limit of photovoltaic conversion. A procedure for calculating the efficiency limit for any irradiance spectrum is presented, without recourse to the Shockley diode equation and taking into account thermal radiation. Simulations were conducted for AM1.5G and selected white LED illumination. The resulting efficiency limit curves show the optimal bandgap pairs for a given irradiance spectrum. Our analysis indicates that the thermodynamic efficiency limit for AM1.5G increases from 33.8 % for a single-junction photovoltaic cell to 45.5 % for a double-junction photovoltaic cell, whereas for LED lighting this increase ranges only from 52.8 % - 54.8 % to 60.6 % - 60.9 %. Replacing single-junction cells with double-junction cells in solar panels can lead to a significant increase in cell output power if the energy gaps of both subcells are properly selected. The range of energy gaps for which the efficiency limit exceeds 40% is quite wide. On the other hand, for indoor photovoltaic cells, there is little benefit from replacing single-junction cells with double-junction cells, while optimizing single-junction cells can yield significant efficiency gains.
